solutions.name: Banking
solutions.tagline: In banking there is no acceptable error rate. Money either moves correctly or it does not, and every transaction becomes a record someone may be asked to explain years later. That is why replacing a core system is rarely a coding problem. It is a matching problem: every interest calculation, every fee and every transfer has to give exactly the same result on the new platform as on the old one. Most teams still check that by hand, in spreadsheets, sprint after sprint. RabbitQA runs that matching autonomously, every scenario, every sprint, and keeps each result as a record you can explain years later.

So testing runs on a subset, on someone's machine, against an extract that arrived three weeks ago. RabbitQA runs the full suite inside your perimeter, on GDPR-safe synthetic data, so proof no longer waits for an extract.

faqs.answer: Yes. AutoRunner executes scenarios in parallel across distributed infrastructure rather than sequentially, so suite duration scales with capacity instead of scenario count. Booking, check-in, manage-booking and profile flows run concurrently across web, mobile web, iOS and Android.

faqs.question: How do you validate a PSS migration without downtime?

faqs.question: How long does it take to turn a reservation specification into test scenarios?

faqs.question: Which passenger channels are covered?

faqs.question: Does RabbitQA replace our QA team?

The tests that prove it usually finish the night before the campaign goes live. RabbitQA verifies every channel in one autonomous run, done well before campaign day, not the night before.

hero.title: Everything Quality Needs, Governed in One Place.
hero.subtitle: Covers the full quality lifecycle, on top of the tools and frameworks you already use.

items.title: Requirement Governance
items.body: Anyone can raise a request. Nobody can raise an untestable one.
points: Most platforms in this category enter the lifecycle at test execution. By then the requirement has already been written, estimated and built. RabbitQA starts earlier. The agent reads whatever arrives, a Word document, a Confluence page, a sixty-page specification, and asks the questions a senior analyst would ask. What is missing. What contradicts what. What nobody can actually test.

The requirement that comes back is scored on clarity, completeness, acceptance criteria and technical detail, and a named person approves it before a sprint commits to anything. Reject it and the reason is on the record.

items.title: AI-Powered Test Generation
items.body: Most generators need a finished user story to work from. This one takes the specification, the Confluence page, the screenshot or the page URL, whatever the requirement actually lives in.
points: Point it at the source and the cases come back written: happy paths, edge cases and negative scenarios, each with preconditions, steps and expected results. A test case a human can run and a runner can automate.

When the requirement changes, you regenerate against the new version and see the old case and the new one side by side before either wins. Comparing two versions of a specification also surfaces the regression coverage the change now needs. That is the part that decides whether your suite is still telling the truth a year from now.

items.title: Orchestrated Execution
items.body: Keep your Selenium suite. Keep your Playwright specs. Keep the pipeline your team already argued about once.
points: RabbitQA orchestrates what you have rather than asking you to rewrite it. Selenium, Gauge, Cucumber, Robot Framework, JUnit, TestNG and xUnit projects run as they are.

Scenarios run against whichever environment you point them at, on runners inside your own network. Failures come back named and stepped, with a screenshot of the state that broke, so the first question in the morning is which step, not which test.
Web, desktop, mobile, API and RoboClick project types. Gauge, Cucumber, Robot, JUnit, TestNG, xUnit, Postman, Recorder and AI Agent frameworks, plus SAP, Oracle and Logo Tiger .

items.title: Cross Platform Coverage
items.body: Web, mobile, desktop, API and physical POS terminals. One workspace, one set of results.
points: 150+ real iOS and Android handsets come as a module rather than a second vendor contract, with session recordings and issue logging straight into Jira and Slack.

And where software-only testing stops, RoboClick keeps going: real card transactions on physical POS hardware. It is the part of a payment journey no browser automation can reach, and it is usually where acceptance defects hide.

items.title: Accessibility Testing and Regulatory Testing
items.body: Accessibility is normally a report someone commissions three weeks before launch, followed by a backlog nobody schedules.
points: Here it runs inside the project rather than beside it. WCAG 2.1 and 2.2 checks execute against your URLs, authenticated pages included, validated against European Accessibility Act requirements. Screen reader coverage across JAWS, NVDA and VoiceOver comes with the engagement, run by our QA team and reported back into the same project as the automated findings.

Every failure comes back with a suggested fix, not just a complaint: the WCAG reference, what to change, and how to verify it. The score is kept per project with its history, so you can see whether the number is moving.

items.title: Production Health
items.body: Most platforms hand you a green pipeline and stop there. The next thing you hear is a customer.
points: HealthCheck stays on after the release. Scheduled checks run against your production endpoints, an incident opens the moment one stops responding, and recurring failures surface as a pattern rather than a series of separate surprises.
Email, Slack and webhook alerts fire on the same event. The first person to hear about an outage is on your team.

items.title: Bring Your Own Model
items.body: Your model, your keys, your contract.
points: Most platforms route every request through their own model, on their own bill. RabbitQA connects to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Gemini or Anthropic, or runs local models entirely on-premise so no prompt leaves your infrastructure.
Your own model usage consumes none of your platform allowance. Your AI cost stays on a contract you negotiated, and you can change model without changing platform.

items.title: Migration and Import
items.body: The coverage you spent three years building does not become a sunk cost because you changed platform.
points: Existing test cases and test sets import from Excel or TestRail. API collections import from Postman, OpenAPI, Swagger, HAR, WSDL or a raw cURL command. Day one starts from your own regression suite rather than an empty workspace.
No migration project. No professional services line item. Your coverage does not start over because your platform did.

items.title: Evidence and Audit
items.body: Every requirement links to its test cases. Every run links to its result. Every approval carries a name and a timestamp.
points: That chain is not a reporting feature bolted on at the end. It is a by-product of how the platform works, which is why it still holds up when someone asks about a release from eight months ago.
When a regulator asks whether a specific rule was tested and who signed it off, the answer is one screen. Most teams answer that question with two to four weeks of manual gathering.
PCI-DSS, PSD2, GDPR, KVKK, EAA, BaFin.
